extraction_notes.note: A \newcommand{\sect} whose body contains \section{#1} is parsed as a heading '1 #1', so every real section is numbered one higher in the facts (Introduction is '2') than in the paper's own cross-references ('section 3' = Cumulant generating function). Section fields follow the facts as required.

Results are written as numbered equations that the text does not name, but the paper argues for them separately (a derivation sentence, Appendix C, an induction). A proves edge needs a result target, so I added a prose claim around the sentence that states each result, with the equation nested inside it.

Appendix C proves the single-channel determinant formula (ClP4) and the N-terminal CGF (ClP5) in one argument. Because a proof counts as each result it proves, a direct ClP4->ClP5 uses edge creates a cycle, so that dependency is recorded only inside PP4's steps.

The Hankel-determinant criterion of Shohat-Tamarkin is stated in full in prose with the determinant as numbered equation (Mo4); kept as an external theorem containing the equation rather than retyping the equation.
Appendix C proves the determinant formula (fe3) and gf6, and in passing re-derives the two-lead gf4. gf4 is a bare equation, so it gets no proves edge, and its \eqref in PSP8 is marked as a mention.
Introduction/conclusion summaries of results, figure captions and experimental remarks are not nodes. Neither is the property that cumulants of independent subprocesses add, which is only applied.

nodes.name: Schrödinger equation on the leads
nodes.statement: \left ({\rm i} {\partial}_t +\frac{1}{2m} {\partial}_x^2\right )\psi (t,x,i) = 0\, ,
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: eqm1

nodes.name: Vertex boundary condition
nodes.statement: \lim_{x\to 0^-}\sum_{j=1}^N \left [\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}-\mathbb U)_{ij} +{\rm i} (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U)_{ij}{\partial}_x \right ] \psi (t,x,j) = 0\, ,
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: bc1

nodes.name: Scattering matrix of the point-like defect
nodes.statement: \mathbb S(k) = -\frac{[\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} - \mathbb U) - k(\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U )]}{[\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} - \mathbb U) + k(\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U)]} \, ,
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: Unitary scattering matrix of the vertex defect, parametrised by U and eta.
nodes.label: S1

nodes.name: Solution field psi
nodes.statement: \psi (t,x,i) = \sum_{j=1}^N \int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{dk}{2\pi } {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \omega (k)t}\, \chi_{ij}(k;x) a_j (k) \, , \qquad \omega(k) = \frac {k^2}{2m} \, .
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: psi1

nodes.name: Scattering wave functions chi
nodes.statement: \chi(k;x) = {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} k x}\, \mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + {\rm e}^{{\rm i} k x}\, \mathbb S(-k)
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.label: chi

nodes.name: Particle current operator
nodes.statement: j(t,x,i)= \frac{{\rm i}}{2m} \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} k}{2\pi} \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} p}{2\pi}\, {\rm e}^{{\rm i} t [\omega(k) - \omega(p)]} \qquad \qquad \qquad \nonumber \\ \times \sum_{l,m=1}^N a^*_l(k) \Bigl \{ \chi^*_{li}(k;x) \left [\partial_{x} \chi_{i m}\right ](p;x) - \left [\partial_{x} \chi^*_{li}\right ](k;x) \chi_{im}(p;x) \Bigr \}a_m(p) \, .
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: Particle current operator on lead i expressed through the oscillators a, a* and wave functions chi.
nodes.label: curr1

nodes.name: Operator Kirchhoff rule
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: The particle currents at the vertex sum to zero.
nodes.label: KR

nodes.name: n-point current correlation function
nodes.statement: {\mathcal W}^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n) = \langle j(t_1,x_1,i) \cdots j(t_n,x_n,i) \rangle_{\beta,\mu}\, ,
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: w1

nodes.name: n-th current cumulant (connected correlator)
nodes.statement: \mathcal C^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n) = \langle j(t_1,x_1,i) \cdots j(t_n,x_n,i) \rangle_{\beta,\mu}^{\rm conn}\, .
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c1

nodes.name: First cumulant (Landauer-Büttiker current)
nodes.statement: {\mathcal W}^i_1 = \mathcal C^i_1 = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{l=1}^N \left (\delta_{il} -|\mathbb S_{il}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2\right ) d_l(\omega) \, , \qquad d_l(\omega)= \frac{1}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}\, .
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c11

nodes.name: Time-integration replacement
nodes.statement: j(t_l,x_l,i) \longmapsto \int_0^T {\rm d} t_l \, j(t_l,x_l,i) \, , \qquad \forall \; l=1,...n\, ,
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c2

nodes.name: Fourier transform of current correlators
nodes.statement: \mathcal Z^i_n(x_1,...,x_n;\nu ) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} {\rm d} \hat{t}_1 \cdots \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} {\rm d} \hat{t}_{n-1} {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \nu (\hat{t}_1+\cdots \hat{t}_{n-1})} \mathcal Z^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n)\, , \qquad \mathcal Z^i_n = {\mathcal W}^i_n,\, \mathcal C^i_n\, ,
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c3

nodes.name: Zero-frequency limit
nodes.statement: \mathcal Z^i_n = \lim_{\nu \to 0^+} \mathcal Z^i_n(x_1,...,x_n;\nu ) \, .
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: c4

nodes.name: Determinant formula for zero-frequency correlator
nodes.statement: {\mathcal W}^i_n=\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{l_1,...,l_n=1}^N \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} \mathbb T^i_{l_1l_1}(\omega)d_{l_1}(\omega )&\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_1}(\omega)d_{l_2}(\omega )&\cdots && \mathbb T^i_{l_nl_1}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ -\mathbb T^i_{l_1l_2}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_1}(\omega )&\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_2}(\omega)d_{l_2}(\omega )& \cdots & &\mathbb T^i_{l_nl_2}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ \vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\ -\mathbb T^i_{l_1l_n}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_1}(\omega )&-\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_n}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_2}(\omega ) & \cdots & &\mathbb T^i_{l_nl_n}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ \end{array}\right | \, ,
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: Zero-frequency n-point current correlator as an energy integral of a determinant of T-matrix entries times Fermi factors.
nodes.label: w2

nodes.name: T-matrix T^i
nodes.statement: \mathbb T^i_{lm}(\omega)=\delta_{li} \delta_{mi} - \mathbb S_{li}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, \overline{\mathbb S}_{mi}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, ,
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: T

nodes.name: Complementary Fermi distribution
nodes.statement: \widetilde{d}_l(\omega ) = 1-d_l(\omega)=\frac{{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}\, .
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: T1

nodes.name: Matrices A^i, B^i and D
nodes.statement: {\mathbb A}^i \equiv \mathbb T^i \, {\mathbb D}\, ,\qquad {\mathbb B}^i \equiv \mathbb T^i\, (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}-{\mathbb D})\, ,\qquad {\mathbb D} \equiv {\rm diag}[d_1(\omega),d_2(\omega),...,d_n(\omega)] \, .
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: m1

nodes.name: Trace representation of current cumulants
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1^i &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} {\rm Tr} \left [ {\mathbb A}^i \right ]\, , \\ \mathcal C_n^i &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{\sigma \in {\cal P}_{n-1}} \, {\rm Tr} \left [ {\mathbb A}^i {\mathbb C}^i_{\sigma_1\sigma_2}\cdots {\mathbb C}^i_{\sigma_{n-2}\sigma_{n-1}}{\mathbb B}^i\right ]\, , \qquad n \geq 2\, ,
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: Cumulants as energy integrals of traces of products of A^i, B^i, C^i summed over permutations.
nodes.label: c51

nodes.name: Matrices C^i
nodes.statement: {\mathbb C}^i_{\sigma_i\sigma_{i+1}} = \begin{cases} \, -{\mathbb A}^i \, , & \qquad \sigma_i < \sigma_{i+1}\, , \\ \quad {\mathbb B}^i \, , & \qquad \sigma_i > \sigma_{i+1}\, . \\ \end{cases}
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.label: m2

nodes.name: Two-lead cumulants C_1 to C_6
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau c_1\, , \\ \mathcal C_2 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau (c_2 -\tau c_1^2)\, , \\ \mathcal C_3 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^2 c_1(1-3c_2+2\tau c_1^2) \, , \\ \mathcal C_4 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^2[c_2 -3c_2^2+12\tau c_1^2c_2 - 2\tau c_1^2(2+3\tau c_1^2)]\, , \\ \mathcal C_5 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^3 c_1[1+30c_2^2 -15c_2(1+4\tau c_1^2) + 4\tau c_1^2(5+6\tau c_1^2)]\, , \\ \mathcal C_6 &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau^3 \{c_2[1+15c_2(2c_2-1)] - 2\tau c_1^2[8+15c_2(9c_2-5)] + \nonumber \\ &+&120 \tau^2 c_1^4(3c_2-1) -120\tau^3 c_1^6\}\, ,
nodes.statement_short: Explicit first six two-lead cumulants in terms of tau, c_1, c_2.
nodes.label: ec1

nodes.name: Combinations c_1 and c_2
nodes.statement: c_1(\omega)\equiv d_1(\omega)-d_2(\omega)\, \qquad c_2(\omega)\equiv d_1(\omega)+d_2(\omega)-2d_1(\omega)d_2(\omega)\, ,
nodes.label: dc

nodes.name: Two-lead transmission probability
nodes.statement: \tau(\omega) = |\mathbb S_{12}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2 = \frac{2m\omega (\eta_1-\eta_2)^2 \sin^2 (\theta)}{(2m\omega+\eta_1^2)(2m\omega+\eta_2^2)} \, , \qquad \theta \in [0,2\pi)\, ,
nodes.label: tr

nodes.name: Parameters eta_i
nodes.statement: \eta_i \equiv \eta\, {\rm tan} (\alpha_i)\, , \qquad \alpha_i \in [-\pi/2, \pi/2)\, ,
nodes.label: tr1

nodes.name: Generating function ansatz
nodes.statement: \mathcal C (\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [1+F_{12}(\tau,d_1,d_2)\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda f(\tau)}-1\right ) + F_{21}(\tau,d_1,d_2)\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda f(\tau)}-1\right )\right ] \, ,
nodes.label: gf1

nodes.name: Cumulants from the generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_n = (-{\rm i} \partial_\lambda)^n\, \mathcal C(\lambda ) \vert_{{}_{\lambda =0}}
nodes.label: gft2

nodes.name: Solution for F_12, F_21 and f
nodes.statement: F_{12} = \frac{1}{2}(c_2 + c_1\sqrt{\tau})\, , \qquad F_{21} = \frac{1}{2}(c_2 - c_1\sqrt{\tau})\, , \qquad f=\sqrt{\tau}\, .
nodes.label: gft3

nodes.name: Two-lead cumulant generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C (\lambda ) &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [1+\frac{1}{2}(c_2+c_1\sqrt{\tau})\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \sqrt{\tau}}-1\right ) + \frac{1}{2}(c_2-c_1\sqrt{\tau})\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda \sqrt{\tau}}-1\right )\right ] \nonumber \\ &=&\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} c_1 \sqrt{\tau}\, \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}) +c_2 \left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})-1\right ] \right \} \, .
nodes.statement_short: Two-lead CGF: log of 1 + i c_1 sqrt(tau) sin(lambda sqrt(tau)) + c_2[cos(lambda sqrt(tau))-1], integrated over energy.
nodes.label: gf4

nodes.name: Energy integration of single-channel generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C^i(\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \mathcal C_\omega^i(\lambda )\, ,
nodes.label: tgf

nodes.name: Single-energy-channel measure
nodes.statement: {\rm d} k\, {\rm d} p \longmapsto {\rm d} k\, {\rm d} p\, (2\pi)^2\, \delta \left (\frac{k^2}{2m} - \omega \right ) \delta (k-p)\, ,
nodes.label: fe1

nodes.name: Single-channel current
nodes.statement: j_\omega^i = \sum_{l,m=1}^N a^*_l\, \mathbb T^i_{lm}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, a_m \, ,
nodes.label: curr2

nodes.name: Fermionic oscillator algebra in a single channel
nodes.statement: [a_i\, ,\, a_j^*]_+ = \delta_{ij}\, ,\qquad [a_i\, ,\, a_j]_+ = [a^*_i\, ,\, a_j^*]_+ = 0\, , \qquad \langle a^*_i a_j\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = \delta_{ij} d_j(\omega)\, .
nodes.label: alg

nodes.name: Single-channel cumulant generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_\omega^i(\lambda ) = \ln \langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda j_w^i} \rangle_{\beta,\mu} \, .
nodes.label: gf5

nodes.name: Determinant formula for the single-channel expectation value
nodes.statement: \langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda j_w^i} \rangle_{\beta,\mu} = {\rm det} \left [\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + \left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \mathbb T^i(\sqrt{2m\omega})} -\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} \right ) {\mathbb D}(\omega) \right ]\, , \qquad {\mathbb D}(\omega ) \equiv {\rm diag}[d_1(\omega),d_2(\omega),...,d_n(\omega)] \, ,
nodes.label: fe3

nodes.name: N-terminal cumulant generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C(\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} c_1^{\rm eff} \sqrt{\tau}\, \sin \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}\right ) +c_2^{\rm eff} \left [\cos \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}\right )-1\right ] \right \} \, .
nodes.label: gf6

nodes.name: Total transmission probability
nodes.statement: \tau(\omega) = \sum_{i=2}^N \tau_i (\omega)\, , \qquad \tau_i (\omega) \equiv |\mathbb S_{1i}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2 \, ,
nodes.label: gf7

nodes.name: Effective Fermi distribution
nodes.statement: d_2 (\omega) \longrightarrow d_2^{\rm eff} (\omega) \equiv \sum_{i=2}^N\frac{ \tau_i (\omega)}{\tau(\omega)}\, d_i(\omega) \, ,
nodes.label: gf8

nodes.name: Orbits of scale-invariant S-matrices
nodes.statement: \{{\cal U}\, \mathbb S_d\, {\cal U}^* \; :\; {\cal U} \in U(N),\; \mathbb S_d = {\rm diag}(\pm 1,\, \pm 1,\, ...\, ,\, \pm 1)\}
nodes.label: si1

nodes.name: Variables gamma_j and Lambda
nodes.statement: \gamma_j\equiv{\rm e}^{-\beta\mu_j}\, ,\qquad \Lambda(\lambda ) \equiv {\rm i} \sqrt{\tau}(\gamma_2-\gamma_1)\sin(\lambda\sqrt{\tau}) +(\gamma_2+\gamma_1)\cos(\lambda\sqrt{\tau})\, ,
nodes.label: si2

nodes.name: Scale-invariant two-lead generating function (dilogarithm form)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \mathcal C(\lambda) = \frac{1}{2\pi \beta}\Bigg\{ &{\rm Li}_2\left (-\gamma_1^{-1}\right ) + {\rm Li}_2\left (-\gamma_2^{-1}\right ) \\ -&{\rm Li}_2\left[\frac{-2}{\Lambda(\lambda) - \sqrt{\Lambda^2(\lambda)-4\gamma_1\gamma_2}}\right] - {\rm Li}_2\left[\frac{-2}{\Lambda(\lambda) + \sqrt{\Lambda^2(\lambda)-4\gamma_1\gamma_2}}\right] \Bigg\}\, , \end{split}
nodes.statement_short: Closed form of the two-lead scale-invariant CGF in terms of dilogarithms.
nodes.label: si3

nodes.name: Low-temperature generating function at mu_+=0
nodes.statement: \lim_{\beta \to \infty} \mathcal C (\lambda )\vert_{{}_{\mu_+=0}} = \frac{|\mu_-|}{2\pi} \ln \left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}) + {\rm i}\, \varepsilon (\mu_-)\sqrt{\tau} \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})\right ] \, ,
nodes.label: si4

nodes.name: Low-temperature cumulants C_1 to C_4
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1 = \frac{\tau \mu_-}{2\pi} \, ,\qquad \mathcal C_2 = \frac{\tau (1-\tau)|\mu_-|}{2\pi}\, ,\qquad \mathcal C_3 = \frac{\tau^2(\tau-1) \mu_-}{\pi}\, ,\qquad \mathcal C_4 = \frac{ \tau^2(\tau-1)(1-3\tau) |\mu_-|}{\pi}\, .
nodes.label: si5

nodes.name: Odd cumulants proportional to the current
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_{2n+1}\propto \mathcal C_1\, , \qquad \mu_+=0\, , \quad \beta \to \infty\, ,
nodes.label: prop

nodes.name: Transferred charge Q_T
nodes.statement: Q_T = \int_0^T {\rm d} t\, \langle j(t,x,i)\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = T \mathcal C_1\, .
nodes.label: si6

nodes.name: Effective charge
nodes.statement: Q_T = \frac{ e^2\tau}{2\pi} VT = \frac{ e_{\rm eff}^2}{2\pi} VT\, , \qquad e_{\rm eff}\equiv e \sqrt {\tau}\, ,
nodes.label: si7

nodes.name: Current C_1 for nonzero mu_+
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_1= \frac{\tau \mu_-}{2\pi} + \frac{\tau}{2\pi \beta} \ln \left [\frac{{\rm e}^{\beta \mu_{{}_+}}+{\rm e}^{-\beta \mu_{{}_-}}}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta(\mu_{{}_+}-\mu_{{}_-})}}\right ] \, .
nodes.label: si8

nodes.name: Asymptotic slopes of C_3 and C_4
nodes.statement: \lim_{\mu_-\to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathcal C_3}{\mu_-} = \frac{\tau^2(\tau-1)}{\pi}\, ,\qquad \lim_{\mu_-\to \pm \infty} \frac{\mathcal C_4}{\mu_-} = \pm \frac{ \tau^2(\tau-1)(1-3\tau)}{\pi}\, ,
nodes.label: asymp

nodes.name: Minimal coupling (LLL)
nodes.statement: {\rm i} \partial_x \longrightarrow {\rm i} \partial_x + A(x)\, .
nodes.label: minc1

nodes.name: LLL time-integrated correlator
nodes.statement: \int_0^T {\rm d} t_1\cdots \int_0^T {\rm d} t_n\, \langle j(t_1,x_1,i)\cdots j(t_1,x_1,i)\rangle_{\beta,\mu}
nodes.label: LL0

nodes.name: Delta-localised potential A(x)
nodes.statement: A(x) \sim \lambda\, \delta(x)
nodes.label: minc2

nodes.name: Levitov-Lee-Lesovik generating function
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_{L} (\lambda ) &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left [1+\frac{1}{2}(c_2+\tau c_1)\left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda}-1\right ) + \frac{1}{2}(c_2-\tau c_1)\left ({\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda}-1\right )\right ] \nonumber \\ &=&\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} c_1 \tau\, \sin (\lambda) + \tau c_2 \left [\cos (\lambda ) -1\right ]\right \} \, .
nodes.statement_short: LLL generating function, with lambda entering the exponent without sqrt(tau).
nodes.label: LL1

nodes.name: LLL cumulants C_{L,3} and C_{L,4}
nodes.statement: \mathcal C_{L, 3} &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau c_1(1-3\tau c_2+2\tau c_1^2) \, , \\\ \mathcal C_{L, 4} &=& \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \tau[c_2 -3\tau c_2^2+12\tau^2 c_1^2c_2 - 2\tau c_1^2(2+3\tau^2 c_1^2)]\, ,
nodes.label: LL2

nodes.name: Single-channel moment generating function
nodes.statement: \chi_\omega (\lambda) = 1+ {\rm i} c_1\sqrt{\tau}\, \sin \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau }\right )+ c_2 \left [\cos \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau} \right )-1\right ]\, ,
nodes.label: Mo0

nodes.name: Moment expansion
nodes.statement: \chi_\omega (\lambda) = \sum_{n=0}^\infty \frac{({\rm i} \lambda)^n}{n!}\, m_n
nodes.label: Mo1

nodes.name: Moment problem equation
nodes.statement: m_n = \int_{\cal D} {\rm d} \xi\, \xi^n \varphi (\xi)\, .
nodes.label: Mo3

nodes.name: Hankel determinants
nodes.statement: \mathbb H_n \equiv \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} m_0&m_1&\cdots && m_n\\ m_1&m_2& \cdots & &m_{n+1}\\ \vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\ m_n&m_{n+1}& \cdots & &m_{2n}\\ \end{array}\right | \geq 0\, .
nodes.label: Mo4

nodes.name: Values of the Hankel determinants
nodes.statement: \mathbb H_0 = 1\, , \qquad \mathbb H_1=\tau(c_2-c^2_1\tau)\, , \qquad \mathbb H_2=\tau^3(1-c_2)(c_2^2-c_1^2\tau)\, , \qquad \mathbb H_{n\geq 3} = 0\, .
nodes.label: Mo5

nodes.name: Determinant H_2'
nodes.statement: \mathbb H_2^\prime \equiv \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} m_1&m_2\\ m_2&m_3\\ \end{array}\right | = \tau^2 (c_1\tau -c_2) \leq 0\, ,
nodes.label: Mo4bis

nodes.name: Probability distribution phi(xi)
nodes.statement: \begin{split} \varphi (\xi) &= \int_{-\infty}^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \lambda}{2\pi}\, {\rm e}^{-{\rm i} \lambda \xi}\, \chi_\omega (\lambda ) \\ &=\frac{1}{2}(c_2-c_1\sqrt {\tau})\delta(\xi +e\sqrt {\tau})+(1-c_2) \delta(\xi) + \frac{1}{2}(c_2+c_1\sqrt {\tau})\delta(\xi -e \sqrt {\tau}) \, , \end{split}
nodes.statement_short: Distribution is a sum of three delta functions at 0 and ±e sqrt(tau) with coefficients p_12, p_11, p_21.
nodes.label: Mo7

nodes.name: Normalisation of phi
nodes.statement: \int_{-\infty}^\infty {\rm d} \xi\, \varphi (\xi) = 1
nodes.label: Mo8

nodes.name: Distribution at tau=0
nodes.statement: \varphi (\xi)\vert_{\tau=0} = \delta(\xi)\, .
nodes.label: Mo7b

nodes.name: Low-temperature limit of p_12

nodes.name: Heat reservoirs R_i
nodes.statement: Each of the $N$ semi-infinite leads is attached at infinity to the a heat reservoir $R_i$ with (inverse) temperature $\beta_i$ and chemical potential $\mu_i$.

nodes.name: Point-like defect
nodes.statement: The defect, which drives the system out of equilibrium, is localised in the vertex of the graph and is described by a $N\times N$ unitary scattering matrix $\mathbb S$.
differentia: is localised in the vertex of the graph
is described by a $N\times N$ unitary scattering matrix $\mathbb S$

nodes.name: Schrödinger junction
nodes.statement: Our investigation covers all point-like defects in the vertex, which are compatible with a unitary time evolution in the bulk generated by the Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian. We call these systems Schr\"odinger junctions.
differentia: compatible with a unitary time evolution in the bulk generated by the Schr\"odinger Hamiltonian

nodes.name: Star graph coordinates
nodes.statement: The system in Fig. \ref{fig1} is localised on a star graph with coordinates $\{(x,i)\, ,:\, x\leq 0,\, i=1,...,N\}$, where $x$ denotes the distance from the vertex and $i$ labels the leads.

nodes.name: Particle current j(t,x,i)
nodes.statement: The main object of our investigation is the particle current $j(t,x,i)$ flowing along the leads of the junction.

differentia: flowing along the leads of the junction

nodes.name: Parametrisation of point-like defects by self-adjoint extensions
nodes.statement: Equation (\ref{bc1}) parametrises all self-adjoint extensions of the bulk Hamiltonian $-{\partial}_x^2$ to the whole graph and gives rise to non-trivial one-body interactions, which are described by the scattering matrix \cite{ks-00}-\cite{k-08} \begin{equation} \mathbb S(k) = -\frac{[\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} - \mathbb U) - k(\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U )]}{[\eta (\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} - \mathbb U) + k(\mbox{${\mathbb I}$}+\mathbb U)]} \, , \end{equation} $k$ being the particle momentum.
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
nodes.statement_short: The boundary condition (bc1) parametrises all self-adjoint extensions of -d^2/dx^2 on the star graph; their scattering matrix is S(k).
conclusions: Equation (\ref{bc1}) parametrises all self-adjoint extensions of the bulk Hamiltonian $-{\partial}_x^2$ to the whole graph

nodes.name: Landauer-Büttiker non-equilibrium steady state
nodes.statement: The physical setting, presented in Fig. \ref{fig1}, is nicely described by the Landauer-B\"uttiker (LB) \cite{L-57, B-86} non-equilibrium steady state $\Omega_{\beta, \mu}$, defined in terms of $(\beta_i,\mu_i)$ and $\mathbb S(k)$.
nodes.section: 3.1 Particle current in the presence of defect
differentia: defined in terms of $(\beta_i,\mu_i)$ and $\mathbb S(k)$

nodes.name: n-th current cumulant
nodes.statement: The $n$-th cumulant in $L_i$ is defined by the {\it connected} part of (\ref{w1}), \begin{equation} \mathcal C^i_n(t_1, x_1,...,t_n,x_n) = \langle j(t_1,x_1,i) \cdots j(t_n,x_n,i) \rangle_{\beta,\mu}^{\rm conn}\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state

nodes.name: Zero-frequency correlators are position independent
nodes.statement: We will show below that in this limit the $x_l$-dependence drops out and $\mathcal Z^i_n$ depends exclusively on the scattering matrix $\mathbb S$ and the heat bath parameters $(\beta_l,\mu_l)$.
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: In the zero-frequency limit the correlators lose their x-dependence and depend only on S and the bath parameters.
conclusions: the $x_l$-dependence drops out and $\mathcal Z^i_n$ depends exclusively on the scattering matrix $\mathbb S$ and the heat bath parameters $(\beta_l,\mu_l)$

nodes.name: Derivation of the zero-frequency correlator
nodes.statement: In fact, using the explicit form of the current (\ref{curr1}) and the correlation function (\ref{A6}) in appendix A, after some algebra one finds \begin{eqnarray} {\mathcal W}^i_n=\int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi} \sum_{l_1,...,l_n=1}^N \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} \mathbb T^i_{l_1l_1}(\omega)d_{l_1}(\omega )&\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_1}(\omega)d_{l_2}(\omega )&\cdots && \mathbb T^i_{l_nl_1}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ -\mathbb T^i_{l_1l_2}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_1}(\omega )&\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_2}(\omega)d_{l_2}(\omega )& \cdots & &\mathbb T^i_{l_nl_2}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ \vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\ -\mathbb T^i_{l_1l_n}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_1}(\omega )&-\mathbb T^i_{l_2l_n}(\omega)\widetilde{d}_{l_2}(\omega ) & \cdots & &\mathbb T^i_{l_nl_n}(\omega)d_{l_n}(\omega )\\ \end{array}\right | \, , \end{eqnarray} where\footnote{Here and in what follows the bar indicates complex conjugation} \begin{equation} \mathbb T^i_{lm}(\omega)=\delta_{li} \delta_{mi} - \mathbb S_{li}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, \overline{\mathbb S}_{mi}(\sqrt{2m\omega})\, , \end{equation} $d_l(\omega)$ is the Fermi distribution (\ref{c11}) of the reservoir $R_l$ and \begin{equation} \widetilde{d}_l(\omega ) = 1-d_l(\omega)=\frac{{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}{1+{\rm e}^{\beta_l (\omega -\mu_l)}}\, . \end{equation}
nodes.section: 3.2 Current cumulants in the LB state
nodes.statement_short: Direct computation: insert the current (curr1) and the determinant 2n-point function (A6), then take the zero-frequency limit.

nodes.name: Two-lead generating function reproduces C_4, C_5, C_6
nodes.statement: One can easily check also that (\ref{gf4}) reproduces perfectly the cumulants $\mathcal C_4$, $\mathcal C_5$ and $\mathcal C_6$ as well and represents therefore a valid candidate for the final result in the case of two leads.
conclusions: (\ref{gf4}) reproduces perfectly the cumulants $\mathcal C_4$, $\mathcal C_5$ and $\mathcal C_6$ as well

nodes.name: Energy channels are statistically independent
nodes.statement: The argument in what follows is based on the fact that the particle transport in our system can be separated in statistically independent processes with fixed energy.
conclusions: the particle transport in our system can be separated in statistically independent processes with fixed energy

nodes.name: Energy conservation at the vertex
nodes.statement: In fact, excitations with different energies propagate in the graph in Fig. \ref{fig1} in a fully independent way, because the only interaction, localised in the vertex, leaves the energy invariant (see (\ref{A7})).
nodes.statement_short: The only interaction sits at the vertex and conserves energy, so different energies propagate independently.

nodes.name: Determinant formula for the single-channel generating function
nodes.statement: The expectation value $\langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda j_w^i} \rangle_{\beta,\mu}$ can be evaluated explicitly. The key points of the computation, which leads to the final result \begin{equation} \langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda j_w^i} \rangle_{\beta,\mu} = {\rm det} \left [\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + \left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \mathbb T^i(\sqrt{2m\omega})} -\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} \right ) {\mathbb D}(\omega) \right ]\, , \qquad {\mathbb D}(\omega ) \equiv {\rm diag}[d_1(\omega),d_2(\omega),...,d_n(\omega)] \, , \end{equation} are given appendix C.
nodes.statement_short: The single-channel expectation of exp(i lambda j) equals det[I + (e^{i lambda T^i} - I) D].

nodes.name: N-terminal cumulant generating function
nodes.statement: In the lead $L_1$ one finds \begin{equation} \mathcal C(\lambda ) = \int_0^\infty \frac{{\rm d} \omega}{2\pi}\, \ln \left \{1+ {\rm i} c_1^{\rm eff} \sqrt{\tau}\, \sin \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}\right ) +c_2^{\rm eff} \left [\cos \left (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}\right )-1\right ] \right \} \, . \end{equation} Here \begin{equation} \tau(\omega) = \sum_{i=2}^N \tau_i (\omega)\, , \qquad \tau_i (\omega) \equiv |\mathbb S_{1i}(\sqrt{2m\omega})|^2 \, , \end{equation} is the total transmission probability between the lead $L_1$ and the remaining $N-1$ leads $L_i$ and $c_{1,2}^{\rm eff}$ are obtained from (\ref{dc}) by the substitution \begin{equation} d_2 (\omega) \longrightarrow d_2^{\rm eff} (\omega) \equiv \sum_{i=2}^N\frac{ \tau_i (\omega)}{\tau(\omega)}\, d_i(\omega) \, , \end{equation} which represents an effective distribution where $d_i(\omega)$ with $i\geq 2$ are weighted by the ratios $\tau_i(\omega)/\tau(\omega)\in [0,1]$.
nodes.statement_short: The N-terminal CGF has the two-lead form with tau the total transmission and d_2 replaced by an effective transmission-weighted Fermi distribution.

nodes.name: Classification of scale-invariant point-like defects
nodes.statement: The scale invariant (critical) elements in the family (\ref{S1}) are fully classified \cite{Calabrese:2011ru} and belong to the orbits \begin{equation} \{{\cal U}\, \mathbb S_d\, {\cal U}^* \; :\; {\cal U} \in U(N),\; \mathbb S_d = {\rm diag}(\pm 1,\, \pm 1,\, ...\, ,\, \pm 1)\} \end{equation} of the adjoint action of the unitary group $U(N)$ on the diagonal matrices $\mathbb S_d$.
nodes.statement_short: Critical S-matrices are the U(N)-conjugates of diagonal matrices with entries ±1.
assumptions: The scale invariant (critical) elements in the family (\ref{S1})
conclusions: are fully classified \cite{Calabrese:2011ru} and belong to the orbits

nodes.name: Charge renormalisation by the defect
nodes.statement: We see that switching on the defect ($\tau < 1$) causes a finite renormalisation of the charge $e \longmapsto e_{\rm eff}$ with respect to the case in which the defect is absent ($\tau=1$). This purely quantum phenomenon is induced by the non-trivial reflection probability $(1-\tau)$ from the defect.
nodes.statement_short: A defect with tau<1 renormalises the charge to e sqrt(tau), a quantum effect of reflection.

nodes.name: Parity of C_3 and C_4 in mu_-
nodes.statement: It follows from (\ref{si3}) that for $\mu_+\not=0$ the cumulants $\mathcal C_3$ and $\mathcal C_4$ are respectively odd and even nonlinear functions of $\mu_-$.
conclusions: the cumulants $\mathcal C_3$ and $\mathcal C_4$ are respectively odd and even nonlinear functions of $\mu_-$

nodes.name: Comparison with the Levitov-Lee-Lesovik setting
nodes.statement: As observed already in \cite{LC-03}, the difference between (\ref{gf4}) and (\ref{LL1}) is not surprising, because these results concern two inequivalent settings. Notice in this respect the twofold role of $\lambda$ in \cite{LLL-96} as a coupling constant (\ref{minc2}) and a counting parameter, whereas the system (\ref{eqm1},\ref{bc1}) and the cumulants (\ref{c51},\ref{c52}) are $\lambda$-independent and $\lambda$ enters in (\ref{gf4}, \ref{gf6}) only as an auxiliary parameter in the spirit of conventional generating functions.
nodes.statement_short: gf4 and LLL's formula differ because they describe inequivalent settings; in LLL lambda is both coupling and counting parameter.

nodes.name: Agreement of the two schemes at tau=0 and tau=1
nodes.statement: Nevertheless, comparing (\ref{gf4}) and (\ref{LL1}), we observe that these results coincide when the defect in the junction disconnects the leads ($\tau=0$), or when the defect is absent ($\tau=1$).
assumptions: when the defect in the junction disconnects the leads ($\tau=0$), or when the defect is absent ($\tau=1$)

nodes.name: First two cumulants agree in both schemes
nodes.statement: Moreover, quite remarkably the first two cumulants generated by (\ref{gf4}) and (\ref{LL1}) coincide for any $\tau$.

nodes.name: Higher cumulants differ in powers of tau
nodes.statement: For distinguishing the two settings, one should concentrate on the higher cumulants $\mathcal C_{n\geq 3}$. It turns out that they have the same monomials in $c_1$ and $c_2$, but with different powers of $\tau$.

nodes.name: Moments and cumulants satisfy the standard relations
nodes.statement: One can verify that (\ref{Mo2}) and the cumulants at energy $\omega$, given by the integrands of (\ref{c51}, \ref{c52}) (see also (\ref{ec1}-\ref{ec6})), satisfy the conventional relations between moments and cumulants.

nodes.name: Moment problem for the current distribution
nodes.statement: This fact represents a great technical advantage for solving the moment problem, namely for determining a probability distribution $\varphi (\xi)$ such that \begin{equation} m_n = \int_{\cal D} {\rm d} \xi\, \xi^n \varphi (\xi)\, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: Find a probability distribution phi on a domain D whose moments are the m_n.

nodes.name: Hankel determinant criterion for the Hamburger moment problem
nodes.statement: A necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of $\varphi$ on $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$ is \cite{ST-70} the non-negativity of the Hankel determinants \begin{equation} \mathbb H_n \equiv \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} m_0&m_1&\cdots && m_n\\ m_1&m_2& \cdots & &m_{n+1}\\ \vdots &\vdots & \vdots&& \vdots \\ m_n&m_{n+1}& \cdots & &m_{2n}\\ \end{array}\right | \geq 0\, . \end{equation}
nodes.statement_short: A distribution on R with moments m_n exists iff all Hankel determinants are non-negative.
conclusions: A necessary and sufficient condition for the existence of $\varphi$ on $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$ is \cite{ST-70} the non-negativity of the Hankel determinants

nodes.name: Non-negativity of the Hankel determinants
nodes.statement: Using the explicit form of $c_i$ and that $\tau \in [0,1]$, one can show that $\mathbb H_2$ and $\mathbb H_3$ are non-negative.
assumptions: Using the explicit form of $c_i$ and that $\tau \in [0,1]$

nodes.name: Existence of the probability distribution on R
nodes.statement: Therefore the probability distribution $\varphi$ on $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$ exists.

nodes.name: Reduction to the Hamburger moment problem
nodes.statement: Combining the results of \cite{ST-70} with \begin{equation} \mathbb H_2^\prime \equiv \left | \begin{array}{cccccccc} m_1&m_2\\ m_2&m_3\\ \end{array}\right | = \tau^2 (c_1\tau -c_2) \leq 0\, , \end{equation} one concludes that the domains $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}_+$ and $[a,b]$ are excluded and one il left therefore with the so called Hamburger moment problem ${\cal D}=\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}$.
conclusions: the domains $\mbox{${\mathbb R}$}_+$ and $[a,b]$ are excluded

nodes.name: Distribution is supported on three points
nodes.statement: Moreover, since $\mathbb H_{n\geq 3} = 0$ the general theory \cite{ST-70} implies that $\varphi$ is localised in three different points on the $\xi$-line.
conclusions: $\varphi$ is localised in three different points on the $\xi$-line

nodes.name: Delta coefficients are probabilities
nodes.statement: One can show in addition that the coefficients of the delta distributions in (\ref{Mo7}) take value in the interval $[0,1]$ and have therefore a direct probabilistic interpretation.
conclusions: the coefficients of the delta distributions in (\ref{Mo7}) take value in the interval $[0,1]$

nodes.name: Emission-absorption probabilities p_ij
nodes.statement: The basic microscopic process, which takes place in the system for $\tau\not=0$, is the emission of a particle with energy $\omega$ from a reservoir $R_i$ and its absorption from $R_j$. Let us denote by $p_{ij}$ the relative probability.
differentia: emission of a particle with energy $\omega$ from a reservoir $R_i$ and its absorption from $R_j$

nodes.name: Identification of the three delta terms with p_12, p_11, p_21
nodes.statement: Recalling that $\varphi$ concerns the lead $L_1$, the three terms in (\ref{Mo7}) correspond to the three elementary processes of emission and absorption relative to the reservoir $R_1$, namely: (i) $p_{12}=\frac{1}{2}(c_2-c_1\sqrt {\tau})$ is the probability for a particle to be emitted from $R_1$ and absorbed by $R_2$; (ii) $p_{11}=(1-c_2)$ is the probability for a particle to be emitted from and absorbed by $R_1$; (iii) $p_{21}=\frac{1}{2}(c_2+c_1\sqrt {\tau})$ is the probability for a particle to be emitted from $R_2$ and absorbed by $R_1$.
nodes.statement_short: The three delta coefficients of phi are p_12, p_11=1-c_2 and p_21, the emission-absorption probabilities of R_1.

nodes.name: Disconnected leads give a trivial distribution
nodes.statement: For $\tau=0$ the two leads are disconnected and one expects therefore that $p_{12} = p_{21}=0$ and $p_{11} =1$. This simple physical observation is confirmed by the fact that the three terms in (\ref{Mo7}) collapse in one, namely \begin{equation} \varphi (\xi)\vert_{\tau=0} = \delta(\xi)\, . \end{equation}

nodes.name: Discontinuity of p_ij at tau=0
nodes.statement: The property (\ref{Mo7b}) implies also that as functions of $\tau$ the probabilities $p_{ij}$ are discontinuous at $\tau=0$, when the system divides in two parts.

nodes.name: Distribution in lead L_2 and p_22=p_11

nodes.statement: The $2n$-point function can be expressed in terms of (\ref{A4},\ref{A5}) as a determinant. nodes.name: Inductive proof of the determinant formula
nodes.statement: The validity of \eqref{A6} can be proven by induction. For $n=1$ the determinant correctly reproduces (\ref{A4}). Iterating this step in $\langle \, \cdots \, \rangle'_{\beta,\mu}$ one obtains the Laplace expansion of the determinant in \eqref{A6} along the first row, which concludes the argument.

nodes.name: Computation of the single-channel generating function
nodes.statement: We summarise here the key points of the computation of the expectation value \eqref{fe3} which leads to the basic result \eqref{gf6}. Without loss of generality we concentrate on the lead $L_1$, the extension to other leads being straightforward. The problem consists in computing \begin{equation} \langle{\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda j_\omega^1}\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = \langle {\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda \sum_{i,j=1}^N a_i^*\mathbb T^1_{ij}a_j}\rangle_{\beta,\mu}\, . \end{equation} It is convenient for this purpose to change the basis in the algebra (\ref{alg}) according to \begin{equation} b_i = \sum_{j=1}^N U_{ij}\, a_j \, , \qquad b^*_i = \sum_{j=1}^N a_j^*\, U^*_{ji}\, , \end{equation} where $U$ is the matrix diagonalising $\mathbb{T}^1$ according to (\ref{Tmat1}). In the new basis the expectation value (\ref{C1}) reads \begin{equation} \langle{\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda j_\omega^1}\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = \langle\prod_{j=1}^N{\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda (\mathbb{T}_d^1)_{jj}b_j^*b_j}\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = \langle\prod_{j=1}^N\left[1+\left({\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda (\mathbb{T}_d^1)_{jj}}-1\right) b_j^*b_j\right]\rangle_{\beta,\mu} \, . \end{equation} In the case $N=2$ one has $\mathbb{T}^1_d={\rm diag}(-\sqrt{\tau},\sqrt{\tau})$ and one finds \begin{equation} \begin{split} \langle{\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda j_\omega^1}\rangle_{\beta,\mu} & = {\rm det} \left [\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + \left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \mathbb T^1_d} -\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} \right ) \begin{pmatrix} \langle b^*_1b_1\rangle_{\beta,\mu} & \langle b^*_1b_2\rangle_{\beta,\mu} \\ \langle b^*_2b_1\rangle_{\beta,\mu} & \langle b^*_2b_2\rangle_{\beta,\mu} \end{pmatrix} \right ] \\ & = 1+ {\rm i} c_1 \sqrt{\tau}\, \sin (\lambda \sqrt{\tau}) +c_2 \left [\cos (\lambda \sqrt{\tau})-1\right ]\, . \end{split} \end{equation} Combining (\ref{C4}) with (\ref{gf5},\ref{tgf}) one gets the final result \eqref{gf4}. The extension to a generic $N>2$ is attained by expanding the product in \eqref{C3} and expressing the multiple correlators of the operators $\lbrace b_i,b_i^*\rbrace$ in terms of two-point functions through the analogue of formula \eqref{A6}. One recognises at this point that the series can be re-summed as a determinant \begin{equation} \langle{\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda j_\omega^1}\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = {\rm det} \left [\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + \left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \mathbb T^1} -\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} \right ) {\mathbb D} \right ]\, , \end{equation} where ${\mathbb D}$ is the diagonal matrix (\ref{m1}) of the Fermi distributions of the reservoirs. In the basis in which $\mathbb T^1$ is diagonal the result (\ref{C5}) takes the form \begin{equation} \langle{\rm e}^{{\rm i}\lambda j_\omega^1}\rangle_{\beta,\mu} = {\rm det} \left [\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} + \left ({\rm e}^{{\rm i} \lambda \mathbb T_d^1} -\mbox{${\mathbb I}$} \right ) U\, {\mathbb D}\, U^*\right ]\, . \end{equation} Using the explicit form of $U$, which can be deduced from (\ref{Tmat3}, \ref{Tmat4}), one obtains from (\ref{C6}) the cumulant generating function (\ref{gf6} - \ref{gf8}) in the multi terminal case.
